Set up private phone access

Recommended: use Tailscale.app on this Mac to Serve AutoByteus at a stable private HTTPS MagicDNS URL. Trusted Local LAN HTTP is also available for home/local pairing.

Target mobile URL

After Serve is running, open or paste the mobile shell URL. AutoByteus will normalize it to the server base internally.

https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net/mobile

Use the full MagicDNS hostname/FQDN shown by Tailscale, such as machine.tailnet.ts.net, for the HTTPS Serve URL. IPv4 and IPv6 are useful diagnostics, but they are not the preferred HTTPS certificate hostname.

1. INSTALL AND SIGN IN TO TAILSCALE.APP ON THIS MAC

macOS

Install Tailscale.app, sign in, and use the direct app commands below for Serve.

Use Tailscale.app to sign in and confirm the full MagicDNS hostname/FQDN. AutoByteus only shows copyable commands; it does not run Tailscale or inspect local Tailscale status.

2. RUN TAILSCALE SERVE ON THIS MAC

DOCKER NODE

Start Docker node

Install the Docker launcher once, then create a normal Docker node for local or trusted private-network access.

1. INSTALL LAUNCHER ONCE

MACOS / LINUX

Install autobyteus-docker

Installs or replaces the local launcher and prints direct-path, current-shell PATH, and persistent profile/update or copy-paste setup guidance.

Copy
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AutoByteus/autobyteus-workspace/personal/scripts/public/docker/autobyteus-docker.sh | bash -s -- install

WINDOWS POWERSHELL

Install autobyteus-docker

Installs or replaces the local launcher and prints direct-path, current-shell PATH, and persistent profile/update or copy-paste setup guidance.

Copy
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AutoByteus/autobyteus-workspace/personal/scripts/public/docker/autobyteus-docker.ps1 | iex; autobyteus-docker install"
2. USE DIRECT COMMANDS

After install, these commands run locally and do not download the launcher again.

The launcher keeps private server state in Docker named volumes, publishes the server/browser ports, and creates host-visible workspace and shared-folder bind mounts.

Create Docker node

Pulls the latest image and creates the next indexed Docker container, preferring friendly sequential host ports when available.

Copy
autobyteus-docker new-container

Upgrade all Docker nodes

Recreates all managed containers with each node's saved image ref while keeping named volumes.

Copy
autobyteus-docker upgrade --all

Destroy all Docker nodes

Removes all managed containers and unused old images while keeping named volumes.

Copy
autobyteus-docker destroy --all

Destroy one Docker node

Run autobyteus-docker status first, then replace <node-name> with the exact managed node name. This removes only that node's container and launcher state while keeping named volumes and host workspaces; the freed indexed slot can be reused by the next new-container invocation.

Copy
autobyteus-docker destroy --name <node-name>

Reset Docker nodes

Destroys all managed containers, keeps volumes, then creates a fresh autobyteus-server-0.

Copy
autobyteus-docker reset

Show workspace paths

Prints the host folders backing /home/autobyteus/workspace and /home/autobyteus/shared for all managed nodes by default.

Copy
autobyteus-docker workspace paths

Apply shared workspace to all nodes

Safely recreates managed containers with the new bind mounts while keeping existing named volumes.

Copy
autobyteus-docker workspace apply --all

Inspect Docker storage

Shows private named volumes, host bind mounts, and launcher state for all managed nodes by default.

Copy
autobyteus-docker storage

Show Docker node URLs

Prints Backend, noVNC, VNC, and debug URLs for all managed nodes by default.

Copy
autobyteus-docker urls

Show Docker node status

Lists managed nodes and their current Docker status.

Copy
autobyteus-docker status

Show Docker node logs

Prints recent logs for autobyteus-server-0 unless you pass another node name.

Copy
autobyteus-docker logs

Stop Docker node

Stops autobyteus-server-0 by default without deleting named volumes.

Copy
autobyteus-docker stop

After new-container prints Backend, paste that URL into Add Remote Node and open the Docker node window over your trusted private network. For Phone Access, create the QR there with a verified phone-facing HTTPS or acknowledged trusted private HTTP /mobile URL that the phone can reach.

SHARED NETWORK WORKSPACES

AutoByteus NFS

AutoByteus NFS is an independent host storage service. AutoByteus uses ordinary filesystem paths and does not detect or manage the underlying storage.

1. Install the CLI

Copy only—nothing runs in AutoByteus. Review the installer at the URL shown in the command first, then paste into a host terminal (not an agent container) in an empty working directory. The script is saved there, installs the tool and prints its version; it does not configure storage. Requires curl, a shell and the checksum utility shown below, not a compiler or Homebrew.

Published installer: v0.1.0. The installer selects the matching OS/architecture archive and verifies it.

macOS

macOS 26+ with APFS. ARM64 / x64 downloads; native storage hosting and host connections.

Copy
curl --fail --location --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 \
  'https://github.com/AutoByteus/autobyteus-nfs/releases/download/v0.1.0/autobyteus-nfs-install.sh' \
  -o autobyteus-nfs-install.sh &&
printf '%s  %s\n' '65769690ada27db304d2e0e4bcd6716e6403f86650ca8f1905e26ebde86d25fa' 'autobyteus-nfs-install.sh' | shasum -a 256 -c - &&
bash autobyteus-nfs-install.sh version
Linux

Ubuntu 24.04 with ext4. ARM64 / x64 downloads; native or Linux Docker storage hosting and host connections.

Copy
curl --fail --location --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 \
  'https://github.com/AutoByteus/autobyteus-nfs/releases/download/v0.1.0/autobyteus-nfs-install.sh' \
  -o autobyteus-nfs-install.sh &&
printf '%s  %s\n' '65769690ada27db304d2e0e4bcd6716e6403f86650ca8f1905e26ebde86d25fa' 'autobyteus-nfs-install.sh' | sha256sum -c - &&
bash autobyteus-nfs-install.sh version
2. Choose what this computer does

After installation: create on the storage host, then connect the other computers. These commands are interactive and may request administrator approval.

Create storage once
Copy

On the storage host, choose an existing or new source folder and trusted computers or private subnet. Existing files stay in place; review administrator changes before approving.

~/.local/bin/autobyteus-nfs create
Connect each other computer
Copy

On each other host, paste the connection JSON printed by create. Review and approve the setup. Application and container configuration stays separate.

~/.local/bin/autobyteus-nfs connect
3. Installed commands

Run these only after installing the CLI. Commands use its explicit path, so no PATH setup is needed. Except for version, they may request administrator approval.

Interactive menu
Copy

Open setup or saved-state options without arguments.

~/.local/bin/autobyteus-nfs
Check status
Copy

Report actual host readiness. This can wait while checking storage or the network.

~/.local/bin/autobyteus-nfs status
Reconnect
Copy

Resume saved storage or pending setup with consent. This is not data recovery.

~/.local/bin/autobyteus-nfs reconnect
Detach safely
Copy

Stop users of the mount first, then review and approve detach. Source files and private data are preserved.

~/.local/bin/autobyteus-nfs detach
Show version
Copy

Print the installed version without configuring storage.

~/.local/bin/autobyteus-nfs version
Public CLI documentation and advanced flags (v0.1.0)

Use the printed mount path as an ordinary directory. AutoByteus does not check its mount type or storage identity. For the Docker launcher, choose an operator-managed shared root with shared/ and nodes/<name>/ subdirectories.

Use only on a trusted private network

NFS traffic is unencrypted. Access trusts the allowed computers, not individual users; writes map to the selected nonroot source owner. Connection details are not an access token. Do not expose this service to the public internet.

If storage or the network goes offline, file operations, previews and unrelated work may stall. Restore connectivity before retrying; there is no offline copy or local fallback.

Mac Docker storage hosting and Windows are not supported. The service does not attach or restart application containers. The Docker Guide configures ordinary directory binds separately.

Downloads are available; physical-host, shared-filesystem, independent-client and user testing remains deferred. Availability does not prove host readiness. Checksums do not replace publisher trust, signing or operating-system security checks.
